messages.author: 3b81b47afc99a09a
messages.subject: Parsing error
parts:
Hi All,
I am running a model on a linux cluster (linux Red Hat 64-bits system with R 3.0.1 & Rstan 2.3.0), and I get a parsing error message:

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  :
failed to parse Stan model 'model_LINUX' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE - DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

LOCATION OF PARSING ERROR (line = 59, position = 8):

PARSED:

generated quantities{

real ordered_env_m[Nmark];
real ordered_site_m[Nmark];

ordered

EXPECTED: "[" BUT FOUND:

_env_m<-sort_desc(theta_env);
ordered_site_m<-sort_desc(theta_site);

}

Calls: system.time -> script -> stan -> stan_model -> stanc
Execution halted
Your job has been killed.

It is surprising that I don't obtain the parsing error on my personal computer (under Windows 8 with the same R and Rstan versions).
Moreover, the parsing error message disappears and the model runs well on the cluster when "ordered_env_m" parameters are defined in "transformed parameters" rather than in "generated quantities".

Curious, isn't it?

Louise

Model :

data {  

int<lower=0> Nmark;

vector[Nmark] FST_p1p2;
vector[Nmark] FST_p1p3;
vector[Nmark] FST_p1p4;
vector[Nmark] FST_p2p3;
vector[Nmark] FST_p2p4;
vector[Nmark] FST_p3p4;

}

parameters{

real mu_env_s1;
real mu_env_s2;
real mu_site;
real tau;
real theta_site[Nmark];
real theta_env[Nmark];

}

transformed parameters{

 real<lower=0> sigma;
 sigma<-sqrt(1/tau);

}

model{

  for (m in 1:Nmark)
  {
  FST_p1p2[m]~normal(mu_env_s1+theta_env[m],sigma);
  FST_p1p3[m]~normal(mu_site+theta_site[m],sigma);
  FST_p1p4[m]~normal(mu_site+theta_site[m]+theta_env[m],sigma);
  FST_p2p3[m]~normal(mu_site+theta_site[m]+theta_env[m],sigma);
  FST_p2p4[m]~normal(mu_site+theta_site[m],sigma);
  FST_p3p4[m]~normal(mu_env_s2+theta_env[m],sigma);

  theta_env[m]~normal(0.0,1E5);
  theta_site[m]~normal(0.0,1E5);
  }

 tau~gamma(.001, .001);
 mu_env_s1~normal(0.0, 1E5);
 mu_env_s2~normal(0.0, 1E5);
 mu_site~normal(0.0, 1E5);

}

generated quantities{

real ordered_env_m[Nmark];
real ordered_site_m[Nmark];

ordered_env_m<-sort_desc(theta_env);
ordered_site_m<-sort_desc(theta_site);

}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Parsing error
parts:
It's the Stan version --- you're running RStan 2.3.0 but
we only fixed the issue with variables sharing a prefix
with types ("ordered" is a type) in a later release.

If you can't easily change the Stan version, you can work
around the parsing bug by replacing prefix "ordered_" with
"ord_" or "desc_"

- Bob
